{{2022 Winter Olympics}}

The [[2022 Winter Olympics]], officially known as the XXIV Olympic Winter Games, were a winter multi-sport event held in [[Beijing]], China, from 31 January to 20 February. A total of 2,871 athletes from 91 nations participated in 109 medal events in seven sports across 15 disciplines.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kesting |first1=Amanda |title=Colorado Sent More Athletes to the Winter Olympics Than More Than Half of the Countries Participating |url=https://www.9news.com/article/sports/olympics/colorado-winter-olympics-delegation-size/73-d466dee8-4ba6-454f-b6a1-d35292d61266 |access-date=13 February 2022 |publisher=[[KUSA (TV)|KUSA]] |date=4 February 2022 |archive-date=9 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230409061404/https://www.9news.com/article/sports/olympics/colorado-winter-olympics-delegation-size/73-d466dee8-4ba6-454f-b6a1-d35292d61266 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Edmonds |first1=Charlotte |title=Here's a Guide to New Events Debuting at the Winter Olympics |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/beijing-2022-winter-olympics/heres-guide-new-events-debuting-winter-olympics |access-date=12 September 2022 |agency=[[NBC Sports Philadelphia]] |date=4 February 2022 |archive-date=17 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230217004939/https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/beijing-2022-winter-olympics/heres-guide-new-events-debuting-winter-olympics |url-status=live }}</ref>

Overall 29 nations received at least one medal, and 23 of them won at least one gold medal. Athletes from [[Norway at the 2022 Winter Olympics|Norway]] won the most medals overall, with 37, and the most gold medals, with 16. The latter record was the highest gold medal tally at a single Winter Games.<ref name="Stuhlbarg">{{cite news |last1=Stuhlbarg |first1=Nate |title=Norway Retains Title with most Medals at 2022 Winter Olympics |url=https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/norway-retains-title-most-medals-2022-winter-olympics |access-date=27 March 2022 |agency=[[NBC Sports]] |date=20 February 2022 |archive-date=20 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220220195122/https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/norway-retains-title-most-medals-2022-winter-olympics |url-status=live }}</ref> Host nation [[China at the 2022 Winter Olympics|China]] won nine gold medals surpassing its gold medal tally of five at the [[2010 Winter Olympics|2010 winter edition]].<ref>{{cite web |title=China, Japan Set New Medal Marks in Winter Olympics |url=https://ocasia.org/news/2816-china-japan-set-new-medal-marks-in-winter-olympics.html |publisher=[[Olympic Council of Asia]] |access-date=12 July 2022 |archive-date=17 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230217005811/https://ocasia.org/news/2816-china-japan-set-new-medal-marks-in-winter-olympics.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Athletes from that nation also won 15 medals overall, which eclipsed its record of 11 at both the [[2006 Winter Olympics|2006]] and 2010 winter editions.<ref name="Stuhlbarg" />

Biathletes [[Johannes Thingnes Bø]], [[Quentin Fillon Maillet]], and [[Marte Olsbu Røiseland]], and cross-country skier [[Alexander Bolshunov]] won the most total medals at the games with five each.<ref>{{cite web |title=Beijing 2022 |url=https://www.teamgb.com/competitions/beijing-2022/6dWdXrzU85Vn1jF6ZC9Onl |publisher=[[British Olympic Association]] |access-date=26 February 2022 |archive-date=18 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220318145104/https://www.teamgb.com/competitions/beijing-2022/6dWdXrzU85Vn1jF6ZC9Onl |url-status=live }}</ref> Bø also earned the most gold medals with four.<ref>{{cite news |agency=[[Agence France-Presse]] |title=Norwegian Biathlete Boe Gets Fourth Beijing Olympics Gold Medal |url=https://www.barrons.com/news/norwegian-biathlete-boe-gets-fourth-beijing-olympics-gold-medal-01645189808 |access-date=27 March 2022 |work=[[Barron's (newspaper)|Barron's]] |date=18 February 2022 |archive-date=22 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230222200651/https://www.barrons.com/news/norwegian-biathlete-boe-gets-fourth-beijing-olympics-gold-medal-01645189808 |url-status=live }}</ref> Snowboarder [[Zoi Sadowski-Synnott]] of [[New Zealand at the 2022 Winter Olympics|New Zealand]] won the first Winter Olympic gold medal for that nation.<ref>{{cite news |first1=Bryan Armen |last1=Graham |title=Zoi Sadowski-Synnott Wins New Zealand's First Ever Winter Olympic Gold |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2022/feb/05/zoi-sadowski-synnott-new-zealand-first-winter-olympic-gold-snowboard-beijing-2022-tess-coady |access-date=12 July 2022 |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=5 February 2022 |archive-date=26 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220226175310/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2022/feb/05/zoi-sadowski-synnott-new-zealand-first-winter-olympic-gold-snowboard-beijing-2022-tess-coady |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Germany at the 2022 Winter Olympics|Germany]] achieved a podium sweep in the [[Bobsleigh at the 2022 Winter Olympics – Two-man|men's two-man bobsleigh competition]] with [[Francesco Friedrich]] and [[Thorsten Margis]]	winning gold, [[Johannes Lochner]] and [[Florian Bauer]] earning silver, and [[Christoph Hafer]] and [[Matthias Sommer]] attaining bronze.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Levinsohn |first1=Dan |title=Germany Sweeps Two-Man Bobsled Podium with Friedrich, Lochner, Hafer |url=https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/recap-two-man-final-heats |access-date=19 February 2022 |agency=[[NBC Sports]] |date=15 February 2022 |archive-date=19 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319113128/https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/recap-two-man-final-heats |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Medal table==

{{see also|List of 2022 Winter Olympics medal winners}}
The medal table is based on information provided by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) and is consistent with IOC conventional sorting in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a NOC. The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ostlere |first1=Lawrence |date=11 August 2024 |title=Olympic medal table: USA beat China to top spot at Paris 2024 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2580716.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812015233/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2594580.html |archive-date=12 August 2024 |access-date=12 August 2024 |work=[[The Independent]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Araton |first1=Harvey |date=18 August 2008 |title=A Medal Count That Adds Up To Little |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321004238/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |archive-date=21 March 2023 |access-date=25 July 2024 |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |date=10 August 2024 |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |archive-date=11 August 2024 |access-date=11 August 2024 |work=[[Diario AS]] |language=en-us}}</ref>

Two bronze medals were awarded to [[Daniela Maier]] and [[Fanny Smith]] for a third-place tie in the [[Freestyle skiing at the 2022 Winter Olympics – Women's ski cross|freestyle women's ski cross event]] following a decision by the [[Court of Arbitration for Sport]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tas-cas.org/fileadmin/user_upload/CAS_Media_Release_8741.pdf|title=Court of Arbitration for Sport Media Release|access-date=13 December 2022|publisher=[[Court of Arbitration for Sport]]|date=13 December 2022|archive-date=13 December 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221213171856/https://www.tas-cas.org/fileadmin/user_upload/CAS_Media_Release_8741.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref>
